body: Alex Ovechkin is best known for scoring goals, but on Nov. 19 he made history by setting one up. His neutral-zone pass started the play that ended with Boone Jenner scoring at 9:44 of the third period against Buffalo, and it gave Ovechkin his 763rd career assist.
That moved him one past Nicklas Backstrom for the most in Washington Capitals history. It also completed a sweep: Ovechkin now leads the franchise in games played, goals, assists and points.
## Why fans are buying in

The timing gives this record extra weight. Ovechkin announced on Oct. 5 that 2026-27 will be his last NHL season, so every milestone from here is part of a farewell tour. The record also ties him to his longtime partner. Backstrom set up 279 of Ovechkin's goals, more than any other player, and Ovechkin assisted on 107 of Backstrom's. Passing his old center is a fitting chapter for fans who watched that duo for well over a decade.

His career numbers speak for themselves: 930 goals, the most in NHL history, and 1,693 points in 1,593 games. Washington's 6-3 loss to Buffalo dropped the team to 10-10-0, but the night belonged to Ovechkin.

The win mattered for the team, too. It ended a three-game skid and moved Seattle to 10-8-1. The Kraken also outshot Vancouver 24-5 in the first period, a franchise record for shots in a single period.
